name: Digitigrade Leg Reconstruction
description: Reconstructs the lower leg and foot into a digitigrade configuration — the user walks on their toes with an elevated heel, creating a leg structure resembling that of a dog, cat, or raptor. The modification requires extensive skeletal restructuring: the metatarsal bones elongate, the ankle joint repositions upward, and the calf musculature redistributes to power the new joint configuration. The result is dramatically enhanced jumping ability (2–3 times unmodified height), improved sprinting speed, and a distinctive, predatory gait. The legs are visually striking — the reversed-knee appearance (actually an elevated ankle, but the illusion is convincing) is unmistakable. Crucible Genomics offers cosmetic overlays including scaled skin, fur covering, and talon-tipped toes. The modification is irreversible without replacement prosthetics — the original bone structure is destroyed during reconstruction.
source_organism: Struthio camelus (ostrich, cursorial leg structure), Panthera pardus (leopard, jumping musculature)
procedure: Major skeletal surgery with retroviral bone restructuring, 5 surgical sessions over 4 months + 6 months physical therapy
expression_time: 6–12 months for full skeletal and muscular adaptation
reversibility: Functionally irreversible — return to plantigrade requires prosthetic replacement
side_effects: 6+ months of rehabilitation learning to walk again
Chronic foot pad pain on hard surfaces without specialized footwear
Cannot wear standard shoes — custom footwear or barefoot only
Back pain from altered spinal loading
Joint degeneration accelerated in the modified ankle
social_perception: Radical and polarizing. Digi-mod users are seen as either admirably committed to body autonomy or as people who have 'given up' being human. Employment discrimination is common. The modification has a dedicated subculture with its own fashion, athletics, and social spaces.
story_hooks: A digi-mod runner discovers they can access maintenance corridors and vertical infrastructure that standard-legged humans can't reach — and someone has been using those spaces for something they don't want found

A Crucible Genomics digitigrade installation develops bone spurs that grow into the modified ankle joint, causing excruciating pain — the recall affects 200 users, and Crucible is denying responsibility
